title: Quant artifact schema harmonization and regression actuator
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Define and implement a canonical, versioned quantization artifact contract and a lightweight runtime 'regression actuator' that automatically validates new quant variants (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ) against production performance fingerprints. This ticket covers schema definition, ingestion/transformation logic, signing/pinning metadata, and a telemetry-driven canary comparator that gates publishing to the model catalog. Goal is to reduce silent regressions from new quant artifacts and make pinning decisions reproducible.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable artifact schema (JSON) exists that captures model_version, quant_variant, quant_algorithm, target_precision, kernel_profile, calibration_seed, expected_latency_p50/p95, token_throughput, and sample_accuracy_fingerprint
Ingestion pipeline transforms incoming quant artifacts into the canonical contract and emits a signed manifest that can be pinned against a model version
Regression actuator runs automated canary comparisons (batch of warm inputs + eval prompts) and emits pass/fail with metric deltas and an artifact score
Publishing to the model catalog is blocked by the actuator if accuracy or latency regressions exceed thresholds; manual override requires documented justification in the manifest
End-to-end test that simulates INT8 and GPTQ artifacts and demonstrates detection of a 6% accuracy regression and a 30% p95 latency regression
Telemetry is wired to the Console dashboard with a per-artifact trend and an alert rule for >3 consecutive canary failures
updates: 2026-02-28: Ticket created after spike showing two recent incidents where GPTQ variants increased latency for long-context workloads (incident IRC-2026-02). Proposal drafted for a canonical artifact contract and lightweight validator.

2026-03-03: Design sync with Research (Lena Cho) and Product (Jonah Kim). Decided to include both deterministic fingerprint (accuracy on eval set) and runtime fingerprint (p50/p95, memory footprint) in schema. Trade-off: larger manifests vs debuggability. Chose richer manifest.

2026-03-06: Prototype ingestion lambda implemented (PR #4783). Lambda normalizes metadata fields and computes a hashed signature over the payload. Works for AWQ/GPTQ sample artifacts from bench cluster.

2026-03-09: Telemetry contract reviewed by Observability team. Added metric names: quant_canary.score, quant_canary.delta_accuracy, quant_canary.delta_p95. Ingested into staging Prometheus/ClickHouse dashboard.

2026-03-11: Implemented canary comparator service that replays a curated prompt set and compares outputs using exact-match and embedding-similarity thresholds. Early results flagged two AWQ artifacts with semantic drift.
2026-03-13: Security review prelim: signing approach uses existing artifact-signing keys; HSM integration deferred to a follow-up. Created follow-up ticket ENG-34108 for HSM/KMS rollout.
2026-03-14: PR #4832 opened for canary comparator integration with catalog publishing flow. Requesting review from infra and product for gating thresholds and manual-override UX.
notes: Decision: include kernel_profile and batch_behavior in manifest to help kernel selection logic in runtime-1.22; this will simplify rollout fallback heuristics.
Risk: increased manifest size could affect storage and indexing costs. Mitigation: compress older manifests and enforce TTL for per-run telemetry traces.
Follow-ups: ENG-34108 (HSM signing), ENG-34210 (UI for manual override and reasoning capture), ENG-34255 (benchmarks for long-context p95 behavior)
Owner: Ravi will shepherd ingestion and canary comparator; Research to provide curated eval set and similarity thresholds. Product to own publishing policy and manual override UX.
